definitions.meaning: leftovers or bits discarded as waste

explanation.surface: Brawls described as things tossed aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a scrap is a minor fight, and scraps are discarded remnants.

clue.text: To urge standing among the leaders causes amazement

indicators.note: among means one piece sits within the other here

parts.note: leaders, the top performers, are stars

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing upright means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them

explanation.surface: Encouraging people while standing among the top brass astonishes onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' turns EGG upward to GGE, which goes 'among' STARS: STA + GGE + RS.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger someone is to astonish or astound them, so the verb fits.

indicators.note: a conversion changes something into a new form, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describes a relative who has changed faith in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conversion of' rearranges ORIENTAL, which has exactly the same eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a family member, so kin and relation are synonyms.

clue.text: A container about right for wine

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other here

parts.note: a pot is a container

explanation.surface: A vessel near the right-hand side holds some wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts POT around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is a fortified Portuguese wine, an example of the category.

parts.note: free means independent, not controlled
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A self-employed worker is given complete authority.
explanation.definitionFit: A free hand means unrestricted authority to act, the same idea as carte blanche.

parts.note: read whimsically, a booked place in a theatre or train is a parliamentary seat held by a shy, unsociable member

explanation.surface: Housing a stand-offish Member of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: An MP holds a seat in Parliament; 'reserved' also means unsociable, so the phrase means a booked place, read as a shy MP's constituency.
explanation.definitionFit: A booked chair kept for one person is the plain sense; the shy MP's parliamentary place is the joke.

indicators.note: obtainable from means the letters can be taken out of the next word

explanation.surface: Liquor or vigour can be got from the Emerald Isle.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside IR(...)D.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan means flair, vigour and spirit, a direct synonym.

indicators.note: returned means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer

explanation.surface: A plate handed back for the dog's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' turns LAMINA around.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog is one example of a creature, so 'perhaps' marks this as an example.

clue.text: Appear ambivalent, as the French said, over a woman

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: dit is French for said
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: Someone seems undecided about a woman, as a French speaker remarked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places DIT above HER in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to hesitate indecisively, which looks ambivalent.

clue.text: Attract everything to go by river

indicators.note: to go by means to sit next to, so the pieces are placed side by side

parts.note: all means everything
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Draw everyone to travel along the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The URE is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To allure is to entice or tempt, a synonym of attract.

indicators.note: fantastic suggests wildness, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An enthusiast gushes about outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fantastic' rearranges SPACE and ITS. The second 'fantastic' defines: escapist fiction is wholly fanciful.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapist entertainment offers fanciful, unreal diversion, so it is wholly fanciful.

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so the preceding letters are put into new order

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered eccentric proves useless at running things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' rearranges CRANK, NO, USE and AT; 'at' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantankerous means bad-tempered and quarrelsome, the same as irascible.

clue.text: Becomes a holy man for example on retirement

indicators.note: retirement means withdrawing backwards, so the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A man becomes a saint, for instance, once he retires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on retirement' turns ST + EG (STEG) backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Gets as in gets old means becomes, a common synonym.

definitions.meaning: a breed of small Scottish terrier
a mound of stones marking a path or summit

explanation.surface: A dog's familiar spot on a walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A cairn terrier is a breed, and a heap of stones is a marker for walkers.

clue.text: Dissolute fellow may be found in the garden shed

definitions.text: may be found in the garden shed

explanation.surface: A debauched man hides among the garden tools.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a libertine, and also a toothed tool kept with garden equipment.

definitions.meaning: the month falls in spring in the northern hemisphere

explanation.surface: Walk somewhere in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: To march is to walk in step, and the third month falls in spring.

clue.text: Being awfully old is really hard

indicators.note: awfully means badly done, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: being, as existence, is the verb is

explanation.surface: Getting terribly old is tough going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges IS and OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid means firm and unyielding, a synonym of very hard.

definitions.meaning: an attic is the highest room in a house
the title of a 1959 British film from John Braine's novel

explanation.surface: A play set in a loft.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the uppermost room, and the phrase is the title of a famous British film.

definitions.meaning: jokingly, furthest towards the stern, the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone asks who is most unforgiving and most behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of stern means strictest; humorously, it also means nearest a ship's rear.

parts.note: jokingly, the things that hold a pig up are its feet

explanation.surface: Boorish fans at a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigs' feet hold up the animal, and are also sold as food.

parts.note: flats are pieces of theatre scenery, so the man who moves them between acts

explanation.surface: A man moving house from one apartment to another.
explanation.walkthrough: Flats here are painted panels of stage scenery, not apartments.
explanation.definitionFit: A stagehand who moves scenery between scenes is the theatre job described.

parts.note: literally the money paid to release a captive

explanation.surface: A slogan about the cost of liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Money demanded for releasing a hostage is literally what buys their liberty.

parts.note: the items to be discussed at a meeting, not places to meet

explanation.surface: Places where people gather.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of items for discussion is what a meeting works through.

clue.text: The ship for gunmen turning over to travel

indicators.note: turning over means the piece is flipped around

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A vessel for armed men capsizes on its journey.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, is turned over to AR. Jason sailed the Argo in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the famous ship of Jason and the Argonauts.

clue.text: A composer some people hardly know

indicators.note: some means only part of the words are used here

explanation.surface: A composer few people have heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across peop(LE HAR)dly.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehar was the Hungarian composer of The Merry Widow.

parts.note: determination like small stones, combining the gravel sense and the courage sense

explanation.surface: Steely, unbending determination.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fine gravel and dogged courage.

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a note is a mark or sign

explanation.surface: A grade arrives for a pupil at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses NOTE in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is the famous English public school near Windsor.

parts.note: a bet is a gamble

explanation.surface: Someone takes a punt with a man from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet.

indicators.note: new material means the letters are made into something fresh

explanation.surface: A contract includes some new content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new material' rearranges CONTAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanction means official approval or permission.

clue.text: To view round about noon is restful

indicators.note: round means one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to see is to view
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Looking around at midday is relaxing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' signals the container; 'noon' as N is a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Serene means calm and peaceful.

clue.text: Lack of generosity can get a girl into trouble

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a mess is trouble
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Stinginess could land a young woman in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' signals the container; 'can get' is only a link, and 'trouble' is a noun here, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanness is stinginess, the opposite of being generous.

clue.text: Plant in which many a cut's made

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, many

indicators.note: made means formed from, so the letters are put together anew

parts.note: the possessive s is no letter, but here cut's is taken as the letters

explanation.surface: A plant whose spiny stems get slashed repeatedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges C (100, many), A and CUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cactus is a spiny desert succulent.
